8: import _ from 'lodash';
9: import logger from '@docusaurus/logger';
10: import {matchRoutes as reactRouterMatchRoutes} from 'react-router-config';
11: import {
12:   parseURLPath,
13:   serializeURLPath,
14:   flattenRoutes,
15:   type URLPath,
16: } from '@docusaurus/utils';
17: import {addTrailingSlash, removeTrailingSlash} from '@docusaurus/utils-common';
18: import type {RouteConfig, ReportingSeverity} from '@docusaurus/types';
19: 
20: function matchRoutes(routeConfig: RouteConfig[], pathname: string) {
21:   // @ts-expect-error: React router types RouteConfig with an actual React
22:   // component, but we load route components with string paths.
23:   // We don't actually access component here, so it's fine.
24:   return reactRouterMatchRoutes(routeConfig, pathname);
25: }
26: 
27: type BrokenLink = {
28:   link: string;
29:   resolvedLink: string;
30:   anchor: boolean;
31: };
32: 
33: type BrokenLinksMap = {[pathname: string]: BrokenLink[]};
34: 
35: // The linking data that has been collected on Docusaurus pages during SSG
36: // {rendered page pathname => links and anchors collected on that page}
37: type CollectedLinks = {
38:   [pathname: string]: {links: string[]; anchors: string[]};
39: };
40: 
41: // We use efficient data structures for performance reasons
42: // See https://github.com/facebook/docusaurus/issues/9754
43: type CollectedLinksNormalized = Map<
44:   string,
45:   {links: Set<string>; anchors: Set<string>}
46: >;
47: 
48: type BrokenLinksHelper = {
49:   collectedLinks: CollectedLinksNormalized;
50:   isPathBrokenLink: (linkPath: URLPath) => boolean;
51:   isAnchorBrokenLink: (linkPath: URLPath) => boolean;
52: };
53: 
54: function createBrokenLinksHelper({
55:   collectedLinks,
56:   routes,
57: }: {
58:   collectedLinks: CollectedLinksNormalized;
59:   routes: RouteConfig[];
60: }): BrokenLinksHelper {
61:   const validPathnames = new Set(collectedLinks.keys());
62: 
63:   // IMPORTANT: this is an optimization
64:   // See https://github.com/facebook/docusaurus/issues/9754
65:   // Matching against the route array can be expensive
66:   // If the route is already in the valid pathnames,
67:   // we can avoid matching against it
68:   const remainingRoutes = (function filterRoutes() {
69:     // Goal: unit tests should behave the same with this enabled or disabled
70:     const disableOptimization = false;
71:     if (disableOptimization) {
72:       return routes;
73:     }
74:     // We must consider the "exact" and "strict" match attribute
75:     // We can only infer pre-validated pathnames from a route from exact routes
76:     const [validPathnameRoutes, otherRoutes] = _.partition(
77:       routes,
78:       (route) => route.exact && validPathnames.has(route.path),
79:     );
80:     // If a route is non-strict (non-sensitive to trailing slashes)
81:     // We must pre-validate all possible paths
82:     validPathnameRoutes.forEach((validPathnameRoute) => {
83:       if (!validPathnameRoute.strict) {
84:         validPathnames.add(addTrailingSlash(validPathnameRoute.path));
85:         validPathnames.add(removeTrailingSlash(validPathnameRoute.path));
86:       }
87:     });
88:     return otherRoutes;
89:   })();
90: 
91:   function isPathnameMatchingAnyRoute(pathname: string): boolean {
92:     if (matchRoutes(remainingRoutes, pathname).length > 0) {
93:       // IMPORTANT: this is an optimization
94:       // See https://github.com/facebook/docusaurus/issues/9754
95:       // Large Docusaurus sites have many routes!
96:       // We try to minimize calls to a possibly expensive matchRoutes function
97:       validPathnames.add(pathname);
98:       return true;
99:     }
100: 
101:     return false;
102:   }
103: 
104:   function isPathBrokenLink(linkPath: URLPath) {
105:     const pathnames = [linkPath.pathname, decodeURI(linkPath.pathname)];
106:     if (pathnames.some((p) => validPathnames.has(p))) {
107:       return false;
108:     }
109:     if (pathnames.some(isPathnameMatchingAnyRoute)) {
110:       return false;
111:     }
112:     return true;
113:   }
114: 
115:   function isAnchorBrokenLink(linkPath: URLPath) {
116:     const {pathname, hash} = linkPath;
117:     // Link has no hash: it can't be a broken anchor link
118:     if (hash === undefined) {
119:       return false;
120:     }
121:     // Link has empty hash ("#", "/page#"...): we do not report it as broken
122:     // Empty hashes are used for various weird reasons, by us and other users...
123:     // See for example: https://github.com/facebook/docusaurus/pull/6003
124:     if (hash === '') {
125:       return false;
126:     }
127:     const targetPage =
128:       collectedLinks.get(pathname) || collectedLinks.get(decodeURI(pathname));
129:     // link with anchor to a page that does not exist (or did not collect any
130:     // link/anchor) is considered as a broken anchor
131:     if (!targetPage) {
132:       return true;
133:     }
134:     // it's a not broken anchor if the anchor exists on the target page
135:     if (
136:       targetPage.anchors.has(hash) ||
137:       targetPage.anchors.has(decodeURIComponent(hash))
138:     ) {
139:       return false;
140:     }
141:     return true;
142:   }
143: 
144:   return {
145:     collectedLinks,
146:     isPathBrokenLink,
147:     isAnchorBrokenLink,
148:   };
149: }
150: 
151: function getBrokenLinksForPage({
152:   pagePath,
153:   helper,
154: }: {
155:   pagePath: string;
156:   helper: BrokenLinksHelper;
157: }): BrokenLink[] {
158:   const pageData = helper.collectedLinks.get(pagePath)!;
159: 
160:   const brokenLinks: BrokenLink[] = [];
161: 
162:   pageData.links.forEach((link) => {
163:     const linkPath = parseURLPath(link, pagePath);
164:     if (helper.isPathBrokenLink(linkPath)) {
165:       brokenLinks.push({
166:         link,
167:         resolvedLink: serializeURLPath(linkPath),
168:         anchor: false,
169:       });
170:     } else if (helper.isAnchorBrokenLink(linkPath)) {
171:       brokenLinks.push({
172:         link,
173:         resolvedLink: serializeURLPath(linkPath),
174:         anchor: true,
175:       });
176:     }
177:   });
178: 
179:   return brokenLinks;
180: }
181: 
182: /**
183:  * The route defs can be recursive, and have a parent match-all route. We don't
184:  * want to match broken links like /docs/brokenLink against /docs/*. For this
185:  * reason, we only consider the "final routes" that do not have subroutes.
186:  * We also need to remove the match-all 404 route
187:  */
188: function filterIntermediateRoutes(routesInput: RouteConfig[]): RouteConfig[] {
189:   const routesWithout404 = routesInput.filter((route) => route.path !== '*');
190:   return flattenRoutes(routesWithout404);
191: }
192: 
193: function getBrokenLinks({
194:   collectedLinks,
195:   routes,
196: }: {
197:   collectedLinks: CollectedLinksNormalized;
198:   routes: RouteConfig[];
199: }): BrokenLinksMap {
200:   const filteredRoutes = filterIntermediateRoutes(routes);
201: 
202:   const helper = createBrokenLinksHelper({
203:     collectedLinks,
204:     routes: filteredRoutes,
205:   });
206: 
207:   const result: BrokenLinksMap = {};
208:   collectedLinks.forEach((_unused, pagePath) => {
209:     try {
210:       result[pagePath] = getBrokenLinksForPage({
211:         pagePath,
212:         helper,
213:       });
214:     } catch (e) {
215:       throw new Error(`Unable to get broken links for page ${pagePath}.`, {
216:         cause: e,
217:       });
218:     }
219:   });
220:   return result;
221: }
222: 
223: function brokenLinkMessage(brokenLink: BrokenLink): string {
224:   const showResolvedLink = brokenLink.link !== brokenLink.resolvedLink;
225:   return `${brokenLink.link}${
226:     showResolvedLink ? ` (resolved as: ${brokenLink.resolvedLink})` : ''
227:   }`;
228: }
229: 
230: function createBrokenLinksMessage(
231:   pagePath: string,
232:   brokenLinks: BrokenLink[],
233: ): string {
234:   const type = brokenLinks[0]?.anchor === true ? 'anchor' : 'link';
235: 
236:   const anchorMessage =
237:     brokenLinks.length > 0
238:       ? `- Broken ${type} on source page path = ${pagePath}:
239:    -> linking to ${brokenLinks
240:      .map(brokenLinkMessage)
241:      .join('\n   -> linking to ')}`
242:       : '';
243: 
244:   return `${anchorMessage}`;
245: }
246: 
247: function createBrokenAnchorsMessage(
248:   brokenAnchors: BrokenLinksMap,
249: ): string | undefined {
250:   if (Object.keys(brokenAnchors).length === 0) {
251:     return undefined;
252:   }
253: 
254:   return `Docusaurus found broken anchors!
255: 
256: Please check the pages of your site in the list below, and make sure you don't reference any anchor that does not exist.
257: Note: it's possible to ignore broken anchors with the 'onBrokenAnchors' Docusaurus configuration, and let the build pass.
258: 
259: Exhaustive list of all broken anchors found:
260: ${Object.entries(brokenAnchors)
261:   .map(([pagePath, brokenLinks]) =>
262:     createBrokenLinksMessage(pagePath, brokenLinks),
263:   )
264:   .join('\n')}
265: `;
266: }
267: 
268: function createBrokenPathsMessage(
269:   brokenPathsMap: BrokenLinksMap,
270: ): string | undefined {
271:   if (Object.keys(brokenPathsMap).length === 0) {
272:     return undefined;
273:   }
274: 
275:   /**
276:    * If there's a broken link appearing very often, it is probably a broken link
277:    * on the layout. Add an additional message in such case to help user figure
278:    * this out. See https://github.com/facebook/docusaurus/issues/3567#issuecomment-706973805
279:    */
280:   function getLayoutBrokenLinksHelpMessage() {
281:     const flatList = Object.entries(brokenPathsMap).flatMap(
282:       ([pagePage, brokenLinks]) =>
283:         brokenLinks.map((brokenLink) => ({pagePage, brokenLink})),
284:     );
285: 
286:     const countedBrokenLinks = _.countBy(
287:       flatList,
288:       (item) => item.brokenLink.link,
289:     );
290: 
291:     const FrequencyThreshold = 5; // Is this a good value?
292:     const frequentLinks = Object.entries(countedBrokenLinks)
293:       .filter(([, count]) => count >= FrequencyThreshold)
294:       .map(([link]) => link);
295: 
296:     if (frequentLinks.length === 0) {
297:       return '';
298:     }
299: 
300:     return logger.interpolate`
301: 
302: It looks like some of the broken links we found appear in many pages of your site.
303: Maybe those broken links appear on all pages through your site layout?
304: We recommend that you check your theme configuration for such links (particularly, theme navbar and footer).
305: Frequent broken links are linking to:${frequentLinks}`;
306:   }
307: 
308:   return `Docusaurus found broken links!
309: 
310: Please check the pages of your site in the list below, and make sure you don't reference any path that does not exist.
311: Note: it's possible to ignore broken links with the 'onBrokenLinks' Docusaurus configuration, and let the build pass.${getLayoutBrokenLinksHelpMessage()}
312: 
313: Exhaustive list of all broken links found:
314: ${Object.entries(brokenPathsMap)
315:   .map(([pagePath, brokenPaths]) =>
316:     createBrokenLinksMessage(pagePath, brokenPaths),
317:   )
318:   .join('\n')}
319: `;
320: }
321: 
322: function splitBrokenLinks(brokenLinks: BrokenLinksMap): {
323:   brokenPaths: BrokenLinksMap;
324:   brokenAnchors: BrokenLinksMap;
325: } {
326:   const brokenPaths: BrokenLinksMap = {};
327:   const brokenAnchors: BrokenLinksMap = {};
328: 
329:   Object.entries(brokenLinks).forEach(([pathname, pageBrokenLinks]) => {
330:     const [anchorBrokenLinks, pathBrokenLinks] = _.partition(
331:       pageBrokenLinks,
332:       (link) => link.anchor,
333:     );
334: 
335:     if (pathBrokenLinks.length > 0) {
336:       brokenPaths[pathname] = pathBrokenLinks;
337:     }
338:     if (anchorBrokenLinks.length > 0) {
339:       brokenAnchors[pathname] = anchorBrokenLinks;
340:     }
341:   });
342: 
343:   return {brokenPaths, brokenAnchors};
344: }
345: 
346: function reportBrokenLinks({
347:   brokenLinks,
348:   onBrokenLinks,
349:   onBrokenAnchors,
350: }: {
351:   brokenLinks: BrokenLinksMap;
352:   onBrokenLinks: ReportingSeverity;
353:   onBrokenAnchors: ReportingSeverity;
354: }) {
355:   // We need to split the broken links reporting in 2 for better granularity
356:   // This is because we need to report broken path/anchors independently
357:   // For v3.x retro-compatibility, we can't throw by default for broken anchors
358:   // TODO Docusaurus v4: make onBrokenAnchors throw by default?
359:   const {brokenPaths, brokenAnchors} = splitBrokenLinks(brokenLinks);
360: 
361:   const pathErrorMessage = createBrokenPathsMessage(brokenPaths);
362:   if (pathErrorMessage) {
363:     logger.report(onBrokenLinks)(pathErrorMessage);
364:   }
365: 
366:   const anchorErrorMessage = createBrokenAnchorsMessage(brokenAnchors);
367:   if (anchorErrorMessage) {
368:     logger.report(onBrokenAnchors)(anchorErrorMessage);
369:   }
370: }

372: // Users might use the useBrokenLinks() API in weird unexpected ways
373: // JS users might call "collectLink(undefined)" for example
374: // TS users might call "collectAnchor('#hash')" with/without #
375: // We clean/normalize the collected data to avoid obscure errors being thrown
376: // We also use optimized data structures for a faster algorithm
377: function normalizeCollectedLinks(
378:   collectedLinks: CollectedLinks,
379: ): CollectedLinksNormalized {
380:   const result: CollectedLinksNormalized = new Map();
381:   Object.entries(collectedLinks).forEach(([pathname, pageCollectedData]) => {
382:     result.set(pathname, {
383:       links: new Set(pageCollectedData.links.filter(_.isString)),
384:       anchors: new Set(
385:         pageCollectedData.anchors
386:           .filter(_.isString)
387:           .map((anchor) => (anchor.startsWith('#') ? anchor.slice(1) : anchor)),
388:       ),
389:     });
390:   });
391:   return result;
392: }
393: 
394: export async function handleBrokenLinks({
395:   collectedLinks,
396:   onBrokenLinks,
397:   onBrokenAnchors,
398:   routes,
399: }: {
400:   collectedLinks: CollectedLinks;
401:   onBrokenLinks: ReportingSeverity;
402:   onBrokenAnchors: ReportingSeverity;
403:   routes: RouteConfig[];
404: }): Promise<void> {
405:   if (onBrokenLinks === 'ignore' && onBrokenAnchors === 'ignore') {
406:     return;
407:   }
408:   const brokenLinks = getBrokenLinks({
409:     routes,
410:     collectedLinks: normalizeCollectedLinks(collectedLinks),
411:   });
412:   reportBrokenLinks({brokenLinks, onBrokenLinks, onBrokenAnchors});
413: }
